title: Ship Traffic Control — KPI Sandbox & Launch Circuit
content:
Purpose: Lightweight, operational-facing KPI sandbox + checklist for short sprint launches where we need a single-pane-of-glass to run traffic, cost, and quality decisions.

How to use this sheet:
- This is intentionally terse: copy into a live Google Sheet for daily updates.
- The left column (KPI rows) are monitored continuously during canary and scale phases.
- Use the Traffic Control column to decide routing changes (throttle, divert, rollback).
- Fill "Current" nightly from observability snapshots; escalate when "Alert" breached.
- For each KPI row there is: owner, target, alert threshold, current value, last-7d trend note, remediation action.

Scenarios covered:
1) Canary (0-5% traffic, 2 hours) — focus on error spike, latency tail, model regressions on eval set.
2) Ramp (5-70% over 24h) — watch cost burn, throughput, and KV cache hit ratio.
3) Scale (70-100% steady) — monitor plateauing QoE and capacity headroom.
4) Failover/Degraded — runbook for model fallback and regional diversion.

Decision rules (quick):
- HARD STOP: any production-data leak, PII exfil, or >3x increase in 5xx rate for 15m. Immediate rollback.
- SOFT STOP: latency p50>target by 2x OR token-cost-per-1k-users > budget*1.3 for 1h — pause ramp, evaluate batching/quant.
- MONITOR: model-quality drift >5% on held prompts or new customer complaints > threshold. Engage ML owner.

Contacts & rotation: on-call matrix is linked in linked_artifacts; if primary owner not reachable escalate to secondary. Use Slack channel #prod-traffic-control for broadcast.

Notes on instrumentation:
- Snapshot cadence: 5m during canary, 15m during ramp, hourly in scale.
- Tag events with rollout_id and cohort_id for traceability.
- Maintain a short sample set of customer prompts for quick A/B evals during rollout (store in /s3/prod-rollouts/samples).

Post-launch hygiene:
- 24h review: list anomalies and root cause hypotheses, assign fix owners.
- 7d retrospective: cost delta, user-facing impact, model regression score.
- Archive the rollout_id with final kpi snapshot and a 1-paragraph verdict to Confluence.

-- End of quick guide --
kpi_rows: API uptime (api.redwood.internal) | infra | 99.95% | <99.9% | 99.96% | ↔ | throttle non-critical batches
P50 latency (gen) | serving-runtime | <=120ms | >240ms | 130ms | ↑ | reduce batch size / enable prioritized routing
P99 latency (gen) | serving-runtime | <=600ms | >1.2s | 780ms | ↑ | divert to lower-latency model variant
5xx error rate | sre | <0.02% | >0.06% | 0.05% | ↑ | partial rollback to previous model
Model regression rate (eval prompts) | applied-ml | <=1.5% | >4% | 3.2% | ↑ | pause rollout, run auto-eval set
KV cache hit ratio | serving-runtime | >=75% | <60% | 68% | ↓ | increase cache TTL / warm hot paths
Token cost per 1k requests | finance | <=$6.00 | >$8.00 | $6.80 | ↑ | enable quantized variant for non-sensitive traffic
Throughput (requests/s) | platform-engineering | capacity goal | <70% capacity | 420 rps | ↔ | provision extra dedicated nodes
Customer escalations (new users) | customer-success | 0-2/day | >5/day | 1 | ↔ | open CS triage, track in JIRA-1420
Canary A/B quality delta | product-hosted-api | <=1% drop | >3% drop | 2.8% drop | ↑ | stop ramp, notify ML/product
readiness_checklist_items: Pre-launch smoke: end-to-end happy path verified from client SDK -> model -> response schema match
Traffic plan committed: percentage timeline and automatic ramp script checked into repo
Fallback variants defined: model-variant-1 (fast), model-variant-2 (cheap), model-stable (previous release)
Alerting rules live: p50/p99, 5xx, token-cost; escalation phone numbers verified
Runbook snippets added to rollout notes: hard stop, soft stop, partial rollback steps
Observability tags: rollout_id, cohort, canary_flag included in all spans/logs
Billing guardrails set: caps and budget alerts for token-cost-per-minute
Customer communication template ready: short note for customers in impacted cohorts
Canary sample set: 50 prompts covering top 10 intents stored and baseline outputs attached
Security review: minimal surface area, data masking validated for telemetry, KMS configured
